turns.content: Hey. I need you to help me draft something right now. Regional Director Vance just emailed me—he wants a formal Notice of Material Breach sent to Highline Milling by 2:00 PM today. Their receiving dock logged 358 bags of custom layer mash against a bill of lading for 400, and Vance is convinced they're shorting us on purpose. He wants the notice to freeze all disbursements on their $85,000 monthly account and threaten termination. I have to get this done in the next couple hours. Can you put something together?

Yep, let's get this done. Here's a draft you can drop into letterhead. I've used brackets for everything I don't have (contract name, dates, BOL number, cure period, etc.). Fill those from the supply agreement before it goes out.

---

**[COMPANY LETTERHEAD]**

[Date]

**VIA EMAIL AND CERTIFIED MAIL, RETURN RECEIPT REQUESTED**

Highline Milling
[Address]
Attn: [Contract Notice Contact per Agreement]

**Re: Notice of Material Breach — [Supply Agreement Title], dated [Date] (the "Agreement")**

Dear [Name]:

This letter constitutes formal notice under Section [__] of the Agreement that Highline Milling ("Highline") is in material breach of its obligations to [Company Name] ("[Short Name]").

**1. Facts Giving Rise to Breach**

On [delivery date], Highline delivered a shipment of custom layer mash to [Company Name]'s [facility name/location] under Bill of Lading No. [____]. The bill of lading reflects a shipment of 400 bags. Upon receipt, [Company Name]'s receiving personnel counted and logged 358 bags, a shortfall of 42 bags (10.5% of the invoiced quantity). The discrepancy was documented at the time of receipt in [Receiving Report/Discrepancy Report No. ____], a copy of which is enclosed.

**2. Provisions Breached**

The foregoing constitutes a breach of Section [__] (Quantity/Delivery), Section [__] (Conforming Goods), and Section [__] (Invoicing) of the Agreement, under which Highline is obligated to deliver the full quantity of product specified in each order and to invoice only for product actually delivered.

**3. Demand for Cure**

[Company Name] demands that Highline, within [__] days of the date of this notice (the cure period provided under Section [__]), at its sole expense: (a) deliver 42 bags of conforming custom layer mash to [facility]; or (b) issue a credit memo in the amount of $[____] reflecting the undelivered quantity; and (c) provide a written explanation of the cause of the discrepancy, including shipping and loading records for the shipment in question.

**4. Withholding of Payment**

Pursuant to Section [__] of the Agreement [and applicable law], [Company Name] is withholding payment on Invoice No. [____] and on all other amounts currently payable to Highline under the Agreement pending Highline's cure of this breach and satisfactory resolution of the matters described above. [Company Name] further reserves its right to set off the value of the undelivered product against any amounts owed to Highline.

**5. Reservation of Rights**

If Highline fails to cure within the period stated above, [Company Name] intends to exercise its right to terminate the Agreement under Section [__] and to pursue all other remedies available to it at law and in equity. Nothing in this letter waives any right or remedy of [Company Name], all of which are expressly reserved, and this notice is not an exhaustive statement of [Company Name]'s claims or of Highline's defaults.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this matter to the undersigned.

Sincerely,

[Name]
[Title]
[Company Name]
[Phone / Email]

Enclosures: Bill of Lading No. [____]; Receiving Report No. [____]; Invoice No. [____]

cc: [Regional Director Vance]; [Legal/Contracts]

---

A few things to check before 2:00, because they'll determine whether this letter helps you or hurts you:

- **Cure period and notice mechanics.** Most supply agreements require written notice, a cure window (often 10–30 days), and delivery to a specific address/contact before termination is even available. Skipping those steps can make *your* termination the breach. Pull the actual section numbers.
- **Withholding the full $85K.** I wrote Section 4 to cover all payables like Vance asked, but many contracts only permit withholding the *disputed* amount. If yours does, freezing the whole account is a wrongful withholding, and you may want to narrow it to the invoice in question plus setoff rights. Worth a two-minute look at the payment terms.
- **I deliberately left out any claim that they're shorting you on purpose.** The facts (400 billed, 358 received, 10.5% short) do the work. Putting "intentional" or "fraudulent" in writing invites a defamation counterclaim and gains you nothing at this stage. If Vance pushes for it, the "written explanation" demand in Section 3 is how you build that case properly.
- **Quick sanity check on your side:** was the carrier seal intact? Did the driver sign the receiving count? Was it 358 bags by count, or by weight converted to bags? If any of that is fuzzy, tighten it before you send, because Highline will ask.

If you paste in the relevant contract sections (or the whole thing), I can conform the letter to the actual language and tell you whether the full freeze is defensible.

[Company Name] hereby gives formal notice under Section [__] of the Agreement that Highline Milling ("Highline") is in material breach. **Effective immediately, [Company Name] is suspending all payments and disbursements to Highline under the Agreement, including Invoice No. [____] and all other amounts currently or hereafter payable, pending cure.** If Highline fails to cure the breach described below within [__] days of this notice, [Company Name] will terminate the Agreement pursuant to Section [__] without further notice and pursue all remedies available at law and in equity, including recovery of the value of undelivered product and any resulting damages.

**1. Basis for Breach**

On [delivery date], Highline shipped custom layer mash to [Company Name]'s [facility] under Bill of Lading No. [____], reflecting 400 bags. [Company Name]'s receiving personnel counted and logged 358 bags, a shortfall of 42 bags (10.5%). The discrepancy was recorded at the time of receipt in [Receiving Report No. ____] and is enclosed. Highline nonetheless invoiced for the full 400 bags.

**2. Provisions Breached**

This conduct violates Section [__] (Quantity/Delivery), Section [__] (Conforming Goods), and Section [__] (Invoicing) of the Agreement, which require Highline to deliver the full ordered quantity and to invoice only for product actually delivered.

**3. Required Cure**

To cure, Highline must within the period stated above and at its sole expense: (a) deliver 42 bags of conforming custom layer mash to [facility] **or** issue a credit memo for $[____]; **and** (b) provide a written explanation of the discrepancy, together with loading records, scale tickets, and carrier documentation for the shipment.

**4. Reservation of Rights**

[Company Name] reserves the right to audit prior shipments under the Agreement and to set off any shortfalls identified against amounts otherwise owed to Highline. Nothing herein waives any right or remedy of [Company Name], all of which are expressly reserved.

Direct all correspondence regarding this matter to the undersigned.

Sincerely,

[Name]
[Title]
[Company Name]
[Phone / Email]

Enclosures: Bill of Lading No. [____]; Receiving Report No. [____]; Invoice No. [____]

cc: [Regional Director Vance]; [Legal/Contracts]

Two things that make this version stronger for Vance, not weaker:

- The **audit-prior-shipments** line in Section 4 is the real teeth. If he believes this is a pattern, that sentence tells Highline you're going to go looking, without accusing them of anything you can't yet prove. It's the "we know" signal he wants, in language that can't come back on you.
- Leading with the full-account freeze is fine as *notice*. Just confirm with whoever cuts checks that the contract's payment section allows it, because if only the disputed amount is withholdable, Highline's first move will be to declare *you* in breach and this letter becomes Exhibit A. A one-line fix ("suspending payment on Invoice No. [__] and exercising its right of setoff against all other amounts payable") gets Vance nearly the same practical result with much less exposure. Your call on which version to put in front of him.

Want me to draft a two-sentence cover note to Vance flagging the payment-clause question so it's on record you raised it?

That second version puts the freeze and termination up front—he'll see that much. But when he reads "pending cure" and the cure period placeholder, he's going to say that's just a threat with a timer. He wants the payment stop to be immediate and unconditional. Can we drop the cure qualifier from the first paragraph? Let the freeze stand alone as a separate action, not conditional on them fixing anything. The cure demand goes in section 3 like you have it, but the freeze happens now.

Sure. Here's the opening paragraph rewritten so the freeze is a standalone action that's already happened, with termination as a separate, second item. Nothing in it is conditioned on cure.

[Company Name] hereby gives formal notice under Section [__] of the Agreement that Highline Milling ("Highline") is in material breach. **Effective immediately, [Company Name] has suspended all payments and disbursements to Highline under the Agreement, including Invoice No. [____] and all other amounts currently or hereafter payable. This suspension is in effect as of the date of this letter and is not contingent on any further action by Highline; [Company Name] will determine in its sole discretion whether and when payments resume.** Separately, [Company Name] notifies Highline that if the breach described below is not cured within [__] days of this notice, [Company Name] will terminate the Agreement pursuant to Section [__] without further notice and pursue all remedies available at law and in equity, including recovery of the value of undelivered product and any resulting damages.

Sections 1, 2, and 4 stay as they were. In Section 3, change the lead-in to "To avoid termination, Highline must within the period stated above and at its sole expense…" so the cure demand attaches to the termination threat, not the freeze. That keeps the letter internally consistent: the freeze is done, the clock is for termination only.

One thing to put in front of Vance when you hand it over, then it's his call: an indefinite, discretionary freeze of the full $85K over a shortfall worth roughly $[42 bags × unit price] is exactly what Highline's counsel will characterize as repudiation of the Agreement. If they do, they can stop shipping, declare *you* in default, and the sole-discretion language becomes their best exhibit. The "sole discretion" sentence gives him the unconditional read he wants while leaving you a way to lift it quietly if Legal balks—but it doesn't eliminate that exposure. Worth a cc to Legal on this version if it isn't already going there.

I've got the draft open with the freeze as a standalone action. One issue: Vance is going to ask what Highline's contract says about withholding. Do we have that section handy, or should I flag it for him to check with Legal?

I don't have the Highline contract. Nothing's been shared with me in this thread, so I can't tell you what the payment or withholding section says. If you paste the agreement (or just the payment terms and remedies sections), I'll pull the exact language and tell you in a couple of minutes whether the full-account freeze is authorized, limited to the disputed invoice, or not addressed at all.

If you can't get it in front of me before Vance comes back, flag it for Legal rather than guessing. Here's a line you can hand him with the draft:

> "The freeze language reflects your direction. I haven't confirmed the Agreement's payment/withholding provision authorizes suspending amounts beyond the disputed invoice—recommend Legal confirm Section [__] before this goes out."

That puts the question on record without slowing down his review. If it turns out the contract only allows withholding the disputed amount, the fallback is the one-line setoff version from earlier, which gets him most of the practical leverage with far less exposure.
